title: Invoker selection & argument integrity runbook and regression harness
creator: Maya Patel
description: Goal: Build a repeatable, automated harness that detects regressions in (1) tool/function selection accuracy and (2) argument validation when models or config change. The harness will run as part of model/config canaries and on a nightly regression train. It should produce actionable signals (precision/recall on chooser, arg schema violations, malformed args, missing required args) and create alerts when thresholds are breached. The intent is to catch subtle behavior shifts introduced by model updates, routing-policy tweaks, or runtime optimizations (e.g., quantization, kernel swaps).
acceptance_criteria: A1: Harness executes end-to-end on canary model changes and config diffs producing a standardized JSON report stored in S3 with schema versioning
A2: Tool selection accuracy metric (top-1 accuracy, top-3 recall) computed on labeled eval set; baseline + drift detection rules implemented
A3: Argument integrity checks detect schema mismatch, missing args, type-coercion divergences; false-positive rate < 3% on validation subset
A4: Automated alerts (PagerDuty + Slack) trigger when selection accuracy drops >5% or argument violation rate increases >200% vs baseline
A5: Integration with canary pipeline so a failing harness can block canary promotion and create a rollback playbook link
tasks: T1: Define labeled eval dataset (1000 canonical prompts + expected tool and canonical args) -- owner: Jonah
T2: Implement harness runner that replays prompts, captures model decisions, and validates args against schema registry
T3: Compute metrics and run statistical drift tests (bootstrap CI + population stability index)
T4: Wire output to dashboard (Grafana) and build an alert rule + PagerDuty integration
T5: Add CI job and canary hook; add gating logic to rollout pipeline
T6: Create runbook/incident play for common failures and false positives

implementation_notes: Runner will run in shadow mode against canary flow; requests are replayed with identical headers and routing policies to ensure parity
Argument validation leverages schema-registry v2; we will record both strict validation errors and soft suggestions (e.g., coercions applied by runtime)
We will label a small subset of prompts with acceptable alternative tools to avoid penalizing benign synonyms (use label metadata field 'allowlist_alternatives')
Metric computation: top-1 accuracy, top-k recall, arg-violation-rate, arg-coercion-rate, FP/TP counts. Persist per-run payloads for differential debugging
To reduce noise, implement a debounce window: transient infra-induced spikes (less than 30m) are suppressed unless sustained across 3 consecutive runs
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Eval set may not represent rare customer intents -> Mitigation: periodically sample production traffic for labeling (privacy-preserving) and augment dataset
Risk: False positives from aggressive schema validation -> Mitigation: tier checks into strict vs advisory and tune thresholds before enabling blocking
Risk: Canary runtime discrepancy with production (hardware/kernel differences) -> Mitigation: run harness across matched hardware profiles and record hardware metadata in reports
notes_to_reviewer: When reviewing the prototype PR, focus on the arg-schema adapter and the way exceptions are categorized (hard vs soft). We need reviewers from runtime (kernel team) and SDK to ensure that the replayed requests match production semantics. Contact Jonah for dataset access.
